\chapter{Came and Got Up}
\label{ch:mw-a2-came-and-got-up}
\hlchaptermodality{160}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say that someone came, got up, sat down or arrived, with the ending that agrees with them.}

Complete MW-R160-came-and-got-up: say who came, who got up and who arrived, for a man, a woman and more than one.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{आयो} · \mw{आई} · \mw{आया} (āyo · āī · āyā)}{आयो · आई · आया (āyo · āī · āyā)}]{\mw{आयो}, \mw{आई}, \mw{आया} — came}

\label{lesson:MW-C160-ayo}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{everyone went home}. Then \emph{to come}, \textbf{\mw{आवणो}}, and \emph{he comes every day}.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the past of \mw{आवणो}}]
\textbf{\mw{आयो}}, \textbf{\mw{आई}} and \textbf{\mw{आया}} do for \textbf{\mw{आवणो}} what \textbf{\mw{गयो}}, \textbf{\mw{गई}} and \textbf{\mw{गया}} do for \textbf{\mw{जाणो}}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{राम} \mw{काल} \mw{आयो।}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rām kāl āyo.} — Ram came yesterday.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{मां} \mw{दिनूगै} \mw{आई।}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mā̃ dinūgai āī.} — Mother came early in the morning.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{सगळा} \mw{आथण} \mw{आया।}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sagḷā āthaṇ āyā.} — Everyone came in the evening.
\end{quote}

CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{āīyo}, \textquotedblleft{}he came\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1045).
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{\mw{वो} \mw{बाजार} \mw{सूं} \mw{आयो।}} — \emph{vo bājār sū̃ āyo.} — He came from the market.
  \item \textbf{\mw{राम} \mw{कद} \mw{आयो}?} — \emph{rām kad āyo?} — When did Ram come?
  \item \textbf{\mw{मां} \mw{काल} \mw{आई।}} — \emph{mā̃ kāl āī.} — Mother came yesterday.
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\emph{He came}? (\textbf{\mw{आयो}}.) \emph{She came}, of mother? (\textbf{\mw{आई}}.) \emph{They came}? (\textbf{\mw{आया}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{उठ्यो} · \mw{बैठ्यो} (uṭhyo · baiṭhyo)}{उठ्यो · बैठ्यो (uṭhyo · baiṭhyo)}]{\mw{उठ्यो}, \mw{बैठ्यो} — got up, sat down}

\label{lesson:MW-C160-uthyo}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{to get up}, \emph{to sit} and \emph{to walk}: \textbf{\mw{उठणो}}, \textbf{\mw{बैठणो}}, \textbf{\mw{चालणो}}. Then \emph{Ram came yesterday}.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: -\mw{यो} on a consonant stem}]
A stem that ends in a consonant takes \textbf{-\mw{्यो}} in the past: \textbf{\mw{उठ}}, \textbf{\mw{उठ्यो}}; \textbf{\mw{बैठ}}, \textbf{\mw{बैठ्यो}}; \textbf{\mw{चाल}}, \textbf{\mw{चाल्यो}}; \textbf{\mw{पूग}}, \textbf{\mw{पूग्यो}}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{हूं} \mw{दिनूगै} \mw{उठ्यो।}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hū̃ dinūgai uṭhyo.} — I got up early in the morning.
\end{quote}

For a woman it is \textbf{-\mw{ी}}, and for more than one \textbf{-\mw{्या}}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{मां} \mw{दिनूगै} \mw{उठी।}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mā̃ dinūgai uṭhī.} — Mother got up early in the morning.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{सगळा} \mw{बैठ्या।}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sagḷā baiṭhyā.} — Everyone sat down.
\end{quote}

CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{ūṭhyo}, \textquotedblleft{}stood up\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1907).
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{\mw{राम} \mw{घरै} \mw{पूग्यो।}} — \emph{rām gharai pūgyo.} — Ram reached home.
  \item \textbf{\mw{मां} \mw{घरै} \mw{पूगी।}} — \emph{mā̃ gharai pūgī.} — Mother reached home.
  \item \textbf{\mw{वो} \mw{कोनी} \mw{उठ्यो।}} — \emph{vo konī uṭhyo.} — He didn't get up.
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\emph{He got up}? (\textbf{\mw{उठ्यो}}.) \emph{She got up}? (\textbf{\mw{उठी}}.) \emph{They sat down}? (\textbf{\mw{बैठ्या}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Came and got up — a review}

\label{lesson:MW-R160-came-and-got-up}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{Ram came yesterday}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Ram came yesterday}; \emph{mother came yesterday}; \emph{everyone came in the evening}
  \item \emph{I got up early in the morning}, as a man and then as a woman
  \item \emph{everyone sat down}; \emph{Ram reached home}
  \item \emph{when did Ram come?}; \emph{he came from the market}
  \item \emph{mother went home}; \emph{he didn't get up}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\emph{Came}, for a man, a woman, and more than one? (\textbf{\mw{आयो}}, \textbf{\mw{आई}}, \textbf{\mw{आया}}.) \emph{Got up}? (\textbf{\mw{उठ्यो}}, \textbf{\mw{उठी}}, \textbf{\mw{उठ्या}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
